page: Amazon Web Services c8id.metal-48xl is a bare-metal compute-optimized server powered by dual-socket Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors. The system delivers 96 physical cores and 192 dedicated vCPUs operating at up to 3.9 GHz, supported by 480 MB of shared L3 cache. The architecture features extensive instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory capacity totals 384 GB of system RAM, offering 2.0 GB per vCPU in line with typical compute-intensive allocation profiles.

Integrated hardware includes 11,400 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage and a baseline network throughput of 75 Gbps. The absence of a hypervisor eliminates virtualization overhead, yielding direct access to raw processor and I/O resources. Benchmarks confirm top-tier performance in highly threaded environments, evidenced by a multi-core score of 22,706 in Geekbench and an aggregate PassMark CPU score of 144,818.45. Memory subsystems deliver uncached read bandwidth reaching 599.05 GB/sec.

Instruction accelerators such as AMX enable strong execution in CPU-based AI inference, reaching 337.95 tokens per second for prompt processing on 7B parameter models. Storage and throughput profiles also show top-tier results in Redis operations (272.79 million ops/sec) and database execution. However, with 2 GB of RAM per vCPU, the instance exhibits a compute-to-memory skew that demands careful workload sizing to avoid memory starvation under high concurrency.

Amazon Web Services c8id.metal-48xl is suitable for high-performance computing, large software compilation pipelines, real-time data processing, media rendering, and low-latency database engines that require massive multi-core throughput and attached NVMe scratch storage.
description: Amazon Web Services c8id.metal-48xl is a bare-metal compute-optimized server driven by 96-core, 192-thread Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors operating at 3.9 GHz. Configured with 384 GB of system memory, the instance maintains a 2 GB per vCPU ratio and integrates 480 MB of L3 cache alongside AVX-512 and AMX instruction extensions. It includes 11,400 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage and 75 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Without hypervisor abstraction, this bare-metal platform achieves top-tier results in multi-threaded benchmarks, Clang compilation, and cached I/O operations, such as 272.79 million Redis SET operations per second. CPU-driven inference speeds reach 337.95 tokens per second for prompt processing on 7B models. The server offers dense compute efficiency for CPU-bound tasks, although memory-intensive applications must account for the 2 GB per vCPU allocation. It is well matched for HPC, distributed compilation, real-time analytics, and I/O-intensive database caching.
